title: Rental displacement review and funeral home deferral
subtitle: Also: Compass Kitchener community priorities, Delaware Avenue sidewalks, 2023 business plan, accessibility appointments, audit plans and platinum data certification.
overview: Council directed staff to look at how the City can support residents displaced when rental buildings are redeveloped. The motion, as amended, asks staff to review rental replacement by-laws used elsewhere in Ontario and to work with community stakeholders on tools that could be used right away. Staff are to report back before the end of 2023 {{vote:m11}}.

Council also deferred a decision on a proposed crematorium at a funeral home on Frederick Street until February 27, 2023, at the applicant's request, so the applicant can review parking and design options {{vote:m10}}. Council approved sidewalks on the north side of Delaware Avenue {{vote:m6}}, a zoning change for 525 New Dundee Road {{vote:m9}}, and the 2023 Business Plan project list, subject to budget approval {{vote:m7}}.

Council heard community priorities for the 2023-2026 Strategic Plan from the Compass Kitchener advisory committee. These cover housing affordability, belonging, newcomers, the environment, urban growth, getting around and public engagement. No decision was sought. The City also received a platinum data certification from the World Council on City Data, and council approved the audit plans for 2022 and 2023.

decisions.detail: Staff will recommend ways to support displaced tenants, review rental replacement by-laws elsewhere in Ontario, and work with community stakeholders, reporting back before the end of 2023.
The planning applications were deferred to the February 27, 2023 meeting at the applicant's request to allow time to review parking, building design and Becker Street options.
Sidewalks will be installed on the north side of Delaware Avenue as part of 2023 roadway reconstruction.
Council approved the zoning by-law amendment requested by HIP New Dundee GP Inc.
Council approved the 2023 Business Plan Project List, subject to approval of the 2023 budget.
Eight applicants were appointed to the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee for terms ending December 31, 2026, pending ratification by the partnering municipalities.
Council approved the 2023 Internal Audit work plan.
Council approved the KPMG audit planning report for the year ending December 31, 2022.

debate: On the displacement motion, one councillor asked how it differed from the planned housing study and the regional inclusionary zoning work. Staff said displacement was not in the earlier scope, and the motion reinforces adding it.

One councillor proposed adding a review of rental replacement by-laws, which require a plan for evicted tenants, such as comparable rents. Another proposed funding community groups to support displaced residents.
Staff advised against committing funds before the programs are designed. Council instead agreed to have staff explore partnerships with community stakeholders as part of the 2023 recommendations.

Councillors questioned Compass Kitchener on whether the public's expectations are realistic given limits on municipal jurisdiction. They also discussed closing the loop on engagement, so residents see how their input was used. Compass Kitchener members answered that public education and partnerships with other governments matter.

Delegates urged improved winter maintenance of cycling lanes and called for more action on homelessness. A councillor said housing and homelessness supports fall mainly to the Region, and encouraged the delegate to speak to Regional Council.
